reasons: narrow: The empirical packing count is defined with a floor at \(1\), while the population packing number is \(0\) for an empty thin set.  The unprotected upper comparison is therefore false in that case; retaining \(1\vee J_P\) is the exact correction and leaves all nonempty-profile rates unchanged.

narrow: The oracle logarithm must inherit the corrected unit floor from the empirical-packing comparison.  Replacing \(J_P\) by \(1\vee J_P\) makes the functional defined even when the relevant population thin set is empty and adds only a numerical constant, not a global \(\log n\) term.
